title: Crow Loop Studio was founded on one idea: solve the problem, not just skin the game.
intro: Crows are one of the few non-primate species known to use — and craft — tools to solve problems. That's the studio's namesake, and it's a more honest parallel than "crows like shiny things."

story.title: The short version
story.p1: Crow Loop Studio was founded by Guido Göbbels, a game designer and director with over a decade of experience turning licensed kids' and young-adult IP into HTML5 games that brands, broadcasters, and toy companies can actually ship. The studio is boutique by design: small enough to move fast and stay personally involved in every project, backed by a network of trusted freelancers and studio partners for anything bigger than one person can carry alone.
story.p2: The name works on three levels that all genuinely apply to the work: the game loop, the core repeating unit every game is built from; the feedback loop, the collaborative process at the center of how a project actually runs; and the magic circle — Johan Huizinga's idea that play creates its own bounded space with its own rules. A small nod for anyone in the industry who catches it.

flyingSheep.title: Before Crow Loop: Flying Sheep Studios
flyingSheep.body: For nearly nine years (2014–2024), Guido was at Flying Sheep Studios in Cologne — joining as the studio's first hire and leaving as Design Director. In that time the studio delivered 220+ HTML5 games for brands including LEGO, Barbie, and DreamWorks, and was acquired by iCandy Interactive in 2022. Across a career spanning 150+ projects and 120+ games for 15+ brands, Guido has led international teams of up to 18 people — team-based, large-studio delivery experience that's distinct from the freelance reference work shown in the Portfolio.

superRtl.body: One relationship carries through both chapters: a multi-year working relationship with Super RTL / Toggo, spanning the Flying Sheep years and continuing into Crow Loop Studio's launch pipeline. It's a concrete, ongoing anchor for the kind of broadcaster-side trust this work depends on.

pov.title: Why HTML5 games for brands
pov.body: HTML5 games run instantly, in a browser, on whatever device a kid happens to be holding — no app-store approval, no install friction, no platform lock-in. For a brand campaign with a launch date and a finite ad flight, that's the difference between a game people actually play and one that gets abandoned at the install prompt. It's also fast and affordable to produce well, which matters when the game is one piece of a bigger campaign, not the whole budget.

inProductionEcho: New Crow Loop Studio projects are underway ahead of the studio's official launch on 01.09.2026 — the Portfolio page has the details.
russelOrigin: Aviator goggles for spotting good ideas from up high, a scarf because a crow needs style — that's basically the whole origin story.

thomasRoessig.role: Former Managing Director, Flying Sheep Studios
thomasRoessig.quote: I cannot overstate how critical Mr. Göbbels was to the success of Flying Sheep over the 9 years of his tenure. Our 10-year relationship with our biggest client SUPER RTL would not have been possible without his skill at fostering long-lasting relationships.

robertHeil.role: Head of Operations, Wegesrand GmbH & Co. KG
robertHeil.quote: Exceptional creativity, strong expertise, and outstanding strategic understanding — he grasped complex requirements and turned them into precise, convincingly presented concepts.
